title: Endocrine: when to test and when to treat

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 2, 7, 18, 19 and 24. Each question cites its item. Provisional grouping; review before trusting.

questions.q: A 32-year-old with an A1c of 6.1%. Which intervention best prevents progression to diabetes?
questions.a: An intensive lifestyle and behaviour programme
d: Ninety minutes of strength training a week
questions.why: The Diabetes Prevention Programme model cut new diabetes by 27% over 15 years in one cohort. Dietary pattern evidence, low-carbohydrate included, is weaker.

questions.q: What weight loss do diabetes prevention programmes set as the goal?
questions.why: Reached through a 500 to 1000 kcal daily deficit and 150 minutes of activity a week, of which up to 75 can be strength training.

questions.q: Headache, growing hands and feet, carpal tunnel symptoms, and a 7-mm pituitary adenoma. Which test is abnormal?
questions.why: A somatotroph adenoma. Prolactin would be the test with galactorrhoea and amenorrhoea; a thyrotroph adenoma raises TSH and T4 together.

questions.q: Which features point to a growth hormone-secreting adenoma rather than another type?
questions.why: Menstrual irregularity and proximal weakness occur with several adenoma types and do not discriminate. The three distractors belong to prolactin, cortisol and TSH excess in turn.

questions.q: A pituitary adenoma with weight gain, easy bruising and proximal weakness. Which test confirms the diagnosis?
questions.why: Cushing disease from a corticotroph adenoma. Easy bruising is the feature that separates it from the other adenoma types.

questions.q: TSH 6, free T4 normal, mild symptoms, not pregnant. Which finding would make levothyroxine indicated?
d: A repeat TSH of 6 in six weeks
A repeat TSH of 8 in six weeks
questions.why: A TSH over 10 is the other accepted trigger. Repeating the TSH at 4 to 6 weeks is still right, to confirm the rise is not transient; T3 is not routinely measured.

questions.q: Which persistent symptom is an accepted indication for treating subclinical hypothyroidism?
questions.why: Symptoms alone, however typical, do not earn treatment while the TSH is under 10 and the antibodies are negative.

questions.q: Disruptive hot flashes at 52, previous hysterectomy. What is the most effective treatment?
questions.why: No progestogen is needed without a uterus. Vaginal oestrogen treats vaginal symptoms, not flashes; testosterone does nothing for them; soy evidence is inconsistent.

questions.q: Which non-hormonal drug is FDA-approved for menopausal hot flashes?
questions.why: SSRIs and SNRIs as a class are effective alternatives to oestrogen, but paroxetine is the one that carries the label.

questions.q: Which drugs are first-line for painful diabetic neuropathy?
questions.why: Lidocaine and capsaicin are second-line with less evidence, stimulation has modest benefit, and opioids are avoided in neuropathic pain altogether.
